exposure: Women who had a first-stage cesarean delivery
Stage of labor at time of cesarean delivery (first stage vs. second stage)
Women who had a second-stage cesarean delivery
outcome: Adverse maternal outcomes (intraoperative trauma, atony, blood transfusion, postoperative hospital stay of more than three days)
Adverse perinatal outcomes (5-min APGAR ≤3, admission to NBU, neonatal death)
cohort: 222 women with singleton, cephalic presenting fetuses at term gestation who had intrapartum primary cesarean delivery during active labor
finding: Second-stage cesarean deliveries were associated with a significantly higher risk of both adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes compared to first-stage cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: Second-stage cesarean deliveries were associated with a significantly higher risk of both adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes compared to first-stage cesarean deliveries.
